rv.q: There is so much alchemy here – it just dazzles and dazzles.
Despite a stumble on the late preview to which critics were invited, it’s an astonishing, deeply moving piece of theatre.
These are two immensely powerful and gripping hours; I have quite simply never seen a better production of this play.
There's an almost unbearable heaviness to Ivo van Hove's powerful revival of All My Sons, staged with a crushing gravity.
There is so much alchemy here – it just dazzles and dazzles.
Essiedu is simply superb, leaning into Chris' essential goodness, his trust in a world that is about to be destroyed.

As we watch them all rip themselves and each other apart on a stage littered with red autumn leaves that irresistibly recall memorial poppy fields, this brutal dismantling of the American dream feels more pertinent than ever.
Absolutely striking, it all comes together to create an All My Sons that feels distinct from any production that has come before it, and also has a sense of danger to it.
And here Van Hove has brought together a cast and crew that demonstrate just why the play endures, delivering an exceptional production.
This All My Sons in some ways is comparatively straightforward.
